Um they're committed to winning, easy to work with, and uh just can't thank them enough just for the support through the whole free agent process. Um, also want to thank the pro department, um, analytics, Brandt Tillis and his crew, um, player player engagement, football ops, uh, everybody was awesome. The the coach, Coach Canales and his staff, they were very helpful through the whole process. Uh, so I can't thank everybody enough just for everything they've done, all the hard hard work that they put in. Um, we got a great team here. Um, we were able to retain a lot of our own. Um, go outside the building and sign some free agents that were really excited about. Uh, I felt like, you know, having that depth and, you know, and frontline players um, that we added in free agency. I think it really gives us a lot of flexibility headed into the draft to draft the best available player. Um, so again, I'm just excited about the direction that we're headed, that the franchise is headed. Um, and we're on to the draft now. And, you know, that's another exciting time where we can add really quality players to our roster. And, uh, we're ready to go. So, with that, I'll open it up to any questions. >> We'll kick things off with Darren Gant, followed by Mike Kay. Go ahead. Uh when you look at both those guys physically, how how big they are, um how long they are, um the effort that they play with, the way they prepare, um they were definitely guys that we had our eyes on during free agency, uh me being a former player and and watching them on tape, they have everything that you want in terms of the motor, the effort, the instincts, the range that they play with. Uh, so they they were really good ads for us and and guys that we're really excited about and they're really going to help our defense moving forward. >> Do you ever catch yourself thinking either one of them really? Okay. He kind of reminds me of fill in the blank, somebody you were with or somebody you've seen along the way? >> Uh, not not really. Uh, I don't really have anybody that I would compare them to. I just know they're two guys that I obviously scouted coming out of college that I held in high regard then and to be able to get them in free agency. They're just going to add so much to our defense along with the guys that we already have. Uh we're just really excited about adding them and adding the type of players and leaders that they are in the locker room, the way they prepare, the way they just approach their day-to-day. They're everything that we wanted. Hey Dan. Um, >> what's up Mike? >> Hey, how's it going? You were pretty overt in your desire to to add a more mobile and younger quarterback. You did that with Kenny Picket. There obviously was an agreement on a trade with Philadelphia with Andy Dalton. I know that hasn't been completed yet or at least announced officially. >> Yeah. You had said that Andy didn't mind competing and you had said that you guys were keeping in touch with him. Why trade him now? And what is the outlook for the position heading into the draft? >> Yeah, I think uh we feel good about our quarterback room. Um you know, going going back to Andy, he Andy's a guy that we hold in high regard here. Uh he really helped Bryce, you know, come along as a rookie and you know, into his third year. Um, so Andy just he bought a lot to our franchise. I can't thank him enough for what he bought. Um, and just the the type of man he is as well. So I definitely wish him the best. Um, adding Kenny Picket, I feel like, you know, adding a mobile quarterback, I think in this league, you mobility I think is big in this league. So, I think adding a guy like Kenny Picket that can move outside the pocket if he needs to, create with his legs if he needs to, um, I think those are all things that were really intriguing to us. And heading into the the draft, um, I think, you know, there's there's going to be options there. Whether they're the best player at the time, uh, is yet to be seen, but, you know, if we have the opportunity to add another young guy to the mix, uh, we'll do that. And then you brought in Rasheed Walker and AJ Dylan on on one-year deals, Luke Forner as well. But with the Walker and Dylan signings, obviously you have two players coming off injury there. What is your outlook on Icky a couple of months removed from surgery as well as Jonathan Brooks as he heads into what is an important season for you guys? >> Yeah, those uh you know, Brooks and uh Icky, they're they're making progress. They're with our trainers every day. They're looking good. Uh they're working their butts off. I don't have a timeline on that to update update you with. Um but both those guys, they're headed in a good direction. Um you know, I think those two guys are are guys that, you know, we're looking to to add to our team that they're going to hopefully be healthy at some point. And um you know, we'll just go from there. We'll go with Joe Pson followed by David Newton. >> Hey Dan, good afternoon. >> Hey, what's up Joe? >> Uh, not too much. Um, when you say you don't have a timeline for Icky, is that do you mean that's there's one that you don't want to share publicly? I'm guessing you have one internally that's going to shape how you address the draft. And I wonder if you, you know, could address that with us, how your view and the the franchise's view of Icky's recovery could impact the ability or or potential that you you take a uh tackle. >> Yeah, I think uh timelinewise with Icky, um I I don't have any updates. You know, everybody recovers differently from injuries. He's making really good progress. He looks really good. Um but in terms of timeline, we we don't know that. So obviously um signing Rasheed Walker, you know, we always have to have a backup plan. We always got to be prepared. There's inevitably going to be injuries in this league and and that's for every position. So, um, in terms of adding Rasheed Walker, like, you know, we're excited about him and and what he's going to be able to bring and, you know, I think, uh, that definitely gives time to, you know, recover and, you know, when we get him back, we'll be excited to have him back, but timeline wise, I don't know that. And on on Walker, bringing him on just the one-year deal, does that leave open the possibility to that give you that flexibility that you mentioned in the draft at that position in particular? >> Um, I think it gives us the flexibility to really draft the best available players. Um, so, you know, if a tackle is the best available player, you know, at that point, then so be it. But, um, I think it definitely gives us that flexibility heading into the draft that we can, you know, be aggressive and and add really good players to our team. >> And then lastly on Rasheed, he had a a gun charge in January. How much vetting did you guys do and were you satisfied with what you found out? >> Um, you know, that's a a pending legal matter right now, so I really can't comment on that, but we did our research. >> Thank you. Yep. David. >> Hey Dan, good to see you. Sorry I was having David. I appreciate your time here. Um, with the this whole situation that Joe was asking about with Rasheed and Icky, um, how much what happened with Yash catch you off guard? Um, first off, you know, Yash obviously is a he's a really good person, uh, a player that we did want to bring back. Um, me being in his shoes, uh, as as a former player, um, I really understand what he was going through. He was trying to decide if he wanted to play or not. Uh, caught us a little off guard, but, you know, again, I've been there. I understand what he's thinking. I have a lot of respect for him and his decision. And you know, just like every position in this league, you have to have backup plans. And you know, I think we did a good job pivoting and and adding to that position. >> And you were again, you were pretty emphatic what you wanted to improve. And it seems like you just got everybody you were looking for. I mean, was there was there a miss or something that you didn't get that you kind of on your wish list that you kind of hope to have right now? Yeah, I mean, we felt we feel really good about what we did and what we accomplished in free agency. I think we, you know, definitely hit on who we wanted to hit on and and we're really happy with that. And again, it gives us a lot of flexibility heading into the draft to be able to do what, you know, we want to do and draft the best available players. Mhm. And and have you uh gotten like as far as your draft list, are you planning to bring in 30 now or kind of where you guys are with your uh list of college guys you're looking at? >> Yeah. Yeah, we'll bring in guys on on the 30 visit and you know, we're going to definitely be strategic in who we bring in and why we bring them in. And uh we definitely have a plan and process in place of of who we do want to bring in. And um look forward to seeing those guys and talking to them. Okay. And I appreciate it. And one more question on Jaylen. Um, his story is really interesting. How how concerned were you with the injury history he had? >> Obviously, we do our research and we feel really good about it. Otherwise, we wouldn't have invested the money that we did in him. We know the type of worker he is and and where he is from an injury standpoint. So, we feel really good about him moving forward and and what he's going to bring to our team. Appreciate it. Thanks a lot. >> Yep. >> Alex Zerlo followed by Jeff Hawkins. >> Hello, Dan. Happy Friday. >> What's up, Alex? >> Hey, what's up, man? Um, I you touched on this earlier, but I wanted to ask I wanted wondered if you could elaborate. Why um was Kenny Picket someone that you wanted to bring in uh to Carolina? Yeah, you know, I think Coach Canales, I think Kenny was a guy that coach really wanted to work with and and was fond of in the um evaluation process. Um I'll go back to what I said before, the mobility and and his ability to create with his legs, I think, was a big part of that. um obviously he can throw the ball and and he has a lot of a lot of upside and um I think like every player you know he knows that he can get better at certain things but we're excited about him >> and then I also wanted to ask the same of John Mchky the third wide receiver. >> Yeah. Yeah. Another guy that we're excited to have obviously Bryce is familiar with him. they played together in college and I know Bryce is really fond of him, you know, not only as a player but as a person. Um, I just think it's another, you know, another piece that we can add to our receiver room that adds depth and competition in that room. And, you know, I think that's what we're trying to do at every spot is just add as much depth and competition as we can. >> Great. Thanks. Hey, good afternoon. How you doing? >> Good. How you doing? >> Good. Um, when you and coach took over, uh, the franchise ranked near the bottom in the NFL PA player polls, but now after signing three, you know, immediate starters in free agency and filling key backup positions before the draft, how how much pride are you taking in developing a locker room culture that is attracting top talent to Charlotte again? Yeah, you know, I think uh coach has done a really good job in terms of the culture and you know, you got to give a lot of credit to the players in our locker room as well. Uh we have really great guys in our locker room. They're not only great players, but they're great people and and that's what we're trying to bring in here. We're trying to bring in not only quality football players but quality people and people that impact the community and um you know I think that that's a big part of the culture around here is you know that family atmosphere that we're trying to attract players from the outside they know that when they come into this building that they have full support from ownership myself coach Canales. Um, so we're just trying to build that family atmosphere around here to where hey, you're you're we're not valuing you just solely based on what you do on the field, but we also care about you off the field as well. Um you know guys that you know we think we might be able to get. Um but yeah, we're we're always going to be looking. We're always going to be aggressive. There's always going to be guys out there that you you know that aren't signed that you know you think should be signed that it may be an opportunity for us to get better. And you know, if we feel like they'll make us better, then you know, we'll definitely explore it. >> Thanks. >> Any more questions for Dan? >> Yeah, I got one. This is David again. Dan, were there any anxious moments on that first day or or kind of tell me what they were and what was the emotion because you guys got Jaylen pretty quick. So, obviously there's always going to be anxious moments. There's, you know, there's 31 other teams that you're competing against and, you know, you don't know what's true.
